newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: FKI may intervene in Midopa takeover bid.
newsitem.headline: FKI may intervene in Midopa takeover bid.

text.p: The Federation of Korean Industries may intervene in Shindongbang Corp's hostile takeover bid for Midopa Department Store Co, a senior federation official said on Tuesday.
"We urged the two companies to compromise and are watching developments," federation executive deputy chairman Sohn Byung-doo told reporters. "If they fail we plan to intervene to settle the issue."
The federation, representing the interests of major South Korean corporations, has 470 members.

Midopa became the target of the country's first major hostile takeover bid when Shindongbang and Korea Industrial Co told the Korea Stock Exchange they were considering taking over the retailer. The presidents of Korea Industrial and Shindongbang are brothers.

Regarding hostile takeover bids or attempts to make huge profits from takeover-linked rises in share prices, Sohn said: "We have to actively defend against any hostile takeover bid, especially if initiated by foreigners."
From this year foreign investors are allowed to participate in friendly takeovers.

Shindongbang told the exchange the nation's largest edible oil company and its joint-venture Dongbang Peregrine Securities bought a combined 6.74 percent stake in Midopa in a bid to participate in the management of the retailer.
But a Shindongbang spokesman declined to comment on whether the latest purchase was part of a plan to take over the retailer.
